policy: Explicit, evidenced DOI-level exclusions override historical includes and pending intent. Confirmed production removals may execute immediately only via deletion-only authorized correction gate; new literature admissions are allowed at 08:00 Asia/Shanghai once daily only. Do not treat a queued exclusion as already removed.

items.title: Nonalternating Chain Walking Polymerization Enables In-Chain Ketone Polyolefin Elastomers
items.reason: Explicit user scope correction: this polyolefin-elastomer polymerization article is outside the requested Gallery coverage.
items.evidenceBasis: The repository records this article as nonalternating chain-walking polymerization producing in-chain ketone polyolefin elastomers. It was included under the earlier broad polymer-methodology rule. The user has explicitly excluded this DOI; this is a scope override, not an unsupported claim that the paper contains no synthetic innovation. Publisher full-text access was not obtained in this recheck.
items.challengeReason: The prior inclusion may be defensible under a broad polymerization-methodology collection, but that interpretation does not override the user's explicit DOI-level boundary. Retain the old review for provenance and supersede its include decision without generalizing the exclusion to all polymers.

items.title: Programming Interfacial Function through Alternating Sequence in Amphiphilic Copolymers
items.reason: User-confirmed exclusion: amphiphilic-polymer sequence/interfacial and membrane-function research is not the requested organic-preparative methodology coverage.
items.evidenceBasis: The stored abstract describes cationic alternating copolymers, comparison with gradient/random analogues, outer-membrane permeabilization, hemolytic activity and antibiotic potentiation. The earlier review treated a bulky-monomer/sequence strategy as sufficient inclusion without weighing the article's interfacial and biological-function objective. The user explicitly rejects that scope interpretation.
items.challengeReason: Alternating copolymer formation and post-polymerization modification are real synthetic operations, but their presence alone is insufficient for this Gallery. The demonstrated sequence-function comparison and the user's express exclusion supersede the earlier polymer-methodology include.

items.title: Generative AI designs functional thiolation domains for reprogramming non-ribosomal peptide synthetases
items.reason: Generative protein/domain design and NRPS biosynthetic assembly-line engineering, not general organic preparative reaction methodology.
items.evidenceBasis: The publisher abstract reports AI design of 76 thiolation domains and testing 578 recombinant NRPS variants in vivo; the readouts are domain compatibility, product formation/yield, soluble expression, refolding and thermal stability. The central contribution is context-dependent protein/domain engineering and biosynthetic assembly-line reprogramming, not a general substrate-to-product organic transformation with preparative substrate scope.
items.challengeReason: The presence of peptide products and increased biosynthetic yields does not make every NRPS engineering study an organic-synthesis method. A new broadly preparative biocatalytic transformation or demonstrated chemical total synthesis would be a different case; neither is established by this article's stated principal contribution. The publisher evidence and the user's explicit instruction agree on exclusion.

items.title: Singlet Oxygen From Lattice Oxygen-Adsorbate Hybridization Drives Highly Selective Electrooxidation of Methallyl Alcohol to Methacrolein
items.reason: Explicit user exclusion under the Gallery scope: electrocatalyst-material and reactive-oxygen engineering focused on methallyl-alcohol oxidation, rather than the requested broadly preparative organic methodology.
items.evidenceBasis: The Wiley article identifies a Mn-doped NiMoO4/copper-oxide electrode, coupled lattice/adsorbate oxygen pathways, singlet-oxygen generation and selective methacrolein production. The abstract also reports applications to furfuryl and benzyl alcohols and flow scale-up; therefore this correction does not claim the paper has no substrate extension. The user expressly excludes the article's materials/mechanistic-performance focus.
items.challengeReason: Alcohol-to-aldehyde synthesis and additional alcohol examples are genuine counterevidence to a blanket no-synthesis label. They do not override the user's explicit scope decision. Exclude this DOI without banning all heterogeneous electrosynthesis. Preserve its publisher first-online date, 2026-08-25, so an existing wrong card is corrected even outside the current three-day/seven-day discovery windows.

items.title: Ice-mediated interfacial membrane synthesis of cargo-independent microcapsules
items.reason: User-confirmed DOI exclusion: the principal contribution is ice-template interfacial membrane fabrication and cargo-independent microcapsule function, not the Gallery's general preparative organic synthesis methodology.
items.evidenceBasis: The Nature Synthesis publisher page was read on 2026-10-02. Its abstract describes monomer enrichment in the quasi-liquid layer of ice spheres, confined interfacial amidation forming a polyamide membrane, and release of cargo-loaded capsules on melting. It reports tunable capsule dimensions, permeability and multienzyme/photoenzymatic CO2-to-methanol performance. These are genuine covalent membrane-formation and biocatalytic operations, but the reported primary contribution is fabrication and function of semipermeable compartments. The user explicitly states this DOI is outside scope. Full article and SI substrate tables were not obtained in this recheck.
items.challengeReason: The strongest argument for the previous include is the real interfacial amidation/polymer formation and the demonstrated catalytic cargo. That does not establish a general organic preparative transformation or transferable polymer reaction/chain-architecture method as the main contribution. Counting membrane thickness, capsule size or cargo compatibility as organic substrate scope was the wrong boundary. The user's explicit exclusion supersedes the 2026-10-02 08:00 include without creating a blanket ban on all polymerization or heterogeneous catalysis papers.

scopeAssessment.primaryContribution: Ice-templated fabrication of cargo-independent semipermeable polyamide microcapsules and their compartmentalization performance.
scopeAssessment.preparativeTransformation: Interfacial amidation forms the capsule membrane; this real chemical reaction is acknowledged rather than denied.
scopeAssessment.generalityEvidence: The obtained abstract discusses capsule dimensions and cargo compatibility. Those measures are not evidence for a general organic substrate-to-product preparative method. No unobserved substrate counts or SI claims are asserted.
scopeAssessment.sourceEvidence: Publisher abstract and captions: membrane fabrication/formation, cargo compatibility, permeability and encapsulated photoenzymatic catalysis. Publication date confirmed as 2026-10-01.
scopeAssessment.boundaryChallenge: Real polyamide formation does not automatically qualify a membrane-fabrication article; explicit user DOI exclusion and primary-contribution assessment both require exclusion.

items.title: Development of a Continuous Glycolysis Process for the Recycling of Polyethylene Terephthalate (PET) from Post-Consumer Polycotton Blended Textile Waste
items.reason: User-confirmed DOI exclusion: this continuous PET glycolysis/recycling process is outside the Organic Synthesis Gallery scope.
items.evidenceBasis: The 2026-10-05 prepublish review records the RSC article as a continuous twin-screw glycolysis process for PET in post-consumer polycotton textile waste. The chemical depolymerization is real, but the article's principal contribution is recycling/process engineering of a polymer waste stream rather than a general organic preparative method. The user explicitly states that this DOI does not count for the Gallery.
items.challengeReason: The strongest argument for inclusion is that PET ester bonds are chemically cleaved and the process is scalable. That does not override the user's DOI-level boundary, and this exclusion must not be generalized to all polymerization, depolymerization, or recycling chemistry.
items.evidenceLevel: fresh prepublish publisher abstract/article-specific primary-source evidence plus explicit user DOI decision

scopeAssessment.primaryContribution: Continuous glycolysis/recycling process development for PET in post-consumer polycotton textile waste.
scopeAssessment.preparativeTransformation: PET ester-bond cleavage by glycolysis in a continuous processing setup.
scopeAssessment.generalityEvidence: The prior review cited real waste-stream handling and continuous twin-screw processing, but not a general small-molecule preparative substrate-to-product scope.
scopeAssessment.sourceEvidence: 2026-10-05 prepublish review cites the RSC DOI/article page and records the publisher abstract facts about continuous glycolysis, PET/polycotton feed, and twin-screw extrusion.
scopeAssessment.boundaryChallenge: Chemical depolymerization and scale-up are genuine synthetic chemistry operations, but the explicit DOI-level user decision excludes this process-engineering/recycling article without creating a category-wide ban.
